_note: Public-figure proof fixture. Details are drawn only from widely published public accounts (Walter Isaacson's biography, the 2005 Stanford commencement address, Lisa Brennan-Jobs' memoir Small Fry). No private data, photos, or voice recordings; URLs are placeholders.

scene1Childhood.partnerInCrime: my dad Paul, who gave me my own corner of his workbench in the garage
scene1Childhood.sillyTrouble: pulling pranks at school until a fourth-grade teacher bribed me with candy and a camera kit to start learning
scene1Childhood.weirdObsession: building Heathkit electronics and taking apart anything my dad brought home to see how it worked

scene2TeenFreedom.freedomMachine: a Volkswagen microbus that I later sold to help pay for the very first Apple computer
scene2TeenFreedom.secretTeenIdentity: a kid who skipped the usual crowd to hang around the Hewlett-Packard Explorers Club and trade ideas with Woz

scene3LeapOfFaith.riskOrAdventure: dropping out of Reed College and staying to sit in on a calligraphy class just because it was beautiful
scene3LeapOfFaith.triumphMoment: building the Apple I with Woz in my parents' garage in Los Altos and selling our first fifty boards

scene4Romance.howWeMet: I met your mom Chrisann at Homestead High when we were both teenagers making art and listening to Dylan
scene4Romance.awkwardDateMoment: we spent a summer in a little cabin in the hills above Cupertino with almost nothing to our names
scene4Romance.theMomentIKnew: years later, when you came to live with me as a teenager and I finally got to be your dad up close

scene5LegacyFinale.whatIWishKidsUnderstood: the Lisa computer was named after you, and I should have told you that a long time before I did
scene5LegacyFinale.timeMachineMessageToChildSelf: you can't connect the dots looking forward, so stay hungry and stay foolish
